These appeals are preferred against the judgment and award dated 05th March, 2020 passed in MVC No.2573 of 2017 by the XI Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi (for short hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to with their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. The essential details of the case are as follows:
The petitioner-claimants are the legal heirs of the deceased individual named Vishwanath Kambar.
On 02nd May, 2016, around 4:00 pm, an incident occurred on Chinchali- Chinchali Railway Station Road, situated within the property of Dhanapal.
During this time, Vishwanath was riding his motorcycle with registration number KA-23/EM-0228 along the left side of the road.
Simultaneously, another motorcycle NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB bearing registration number KA-23-CJ-8649, coming from the opposite direction, was being driven recklessly and negligently.

Suddenly,
the latter motorcycle lost control, leading to a collision with Vishwanath.
This collision resulted in Vishwanath suffering severe head injuries along with injuries to crucial parts of his body.
After the accident, Vishwanath was admitted to Wanles Hospital in Miraj for treatment.
Unfortunately, he succumbed to his injuries on 04th May, 2016.

The petition further outlines details concerning the dependency, income,
and other relevant aspects.
The claimants are seeking compensation due to the aforementioned circumstances.
4. Pursuant to service of notice, respondents 1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed objections.

5. The substance of statement of objections of respondent No.1 is that the deceased-Vishwanath was riding unregistered motorcycle without holding Driving Licence and therefore, the charge sheet is filed against him.

Respondents 3 and 4 are residents of Nadi Ingalgaon village in Athani Taluk;
Respondent No.1 is resident of Chinchali village in Belagavi Taluk, the accident took place in Chinchali village limits, and NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB therefore, the Tribunal has no jurisdiction to try this case.
It is further stated that the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 at the time of accident and on these grounds sought to dismiss the petition.

Mahadevi vs Anil @ Anilkumar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156362189/
4 6.
The substance of the statement of objections of respondent No.2 is that there is no nexus between the alleged injuries and the offending vehicle.
Deceased-Vishwanath was riding motorcycle without holding Driving Licence and he had contributed to the alleged accident due to his rash and negligent driving.
The owner and insurer of the vehicle are the necessary parties and hence the petition is bad in law for non- joinder of necessary parties to the petition.
It is also stated that the deceased was not wearing approved headgear; and also denied the other averments made in the petition and accordingly, sought for dismissal for petition.
7. Based on the presented pleadings, the Tribunal had formulated key issues for consideration.

These included determining whether the petitioner could substantiate that on 02nd May, 2016, at approximately 4:00 pm, within the vicinity of Chinchali village and near Dhanapal Handage's land,
an NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB accident had occurred involving Sri Vishwanath, the son of Mallappa Kambar, due to the negligent or rash riding of a motorcycle with registration No.KA-23/EJ-8649.
The Tribunal also aimed to establish if the respondents could successfully prove that the accident was solely a result of the reckless driving of another motorcycle bearing No.KA-23/M-0228.
Additionally, the Tribunal sought to ascertain whether the petitioners were financially dependent on the deceased Vishwanath.
Subsequently, the Tribunal aimed to determine if the petitioners were entitled to receive compensation, and if so, the amount and the liability.
8. To substantiate the case of petitioner, petitioner No.1 had been examined as PW1 and had presented ten documents, designated as Exhibits P1 to P10.

On behalf of the respondents,
respondent No.1 had undergone examination as RW1 and had introduced three documents,
identified as Exhibits R1 to R3.
9.

The Tribunal determined that the petitioner had established that on 02nd May, 2016, around 4:00 pm, within the territorial limits of Chinchali village, adjacent to Dhanapal NC:
2023:KHC-D:9079-DB Handage's property, on the Chinchali-Chinchali Railway Station road, Sri Vishwanath, Mallappa Kambar's son, had been involved in an accident due to the motorcycle bearing No.KA- 23/EJ-8649 being operated negligently or recklessly.
The Tribunal acknowledged the petitioner's entitlement to compensation while acknowledging a contributory negligence in the ratio of 50:50.

The Tribunal also found that the respondents failed to demonstrate that the accident had occurred exclusively due to the rash or negligent operation of the motorcycle with registration No.KA-23/M-0228.
Additionally, the Tribunal ascertained that the petitioner was indeed dependent on the deceased, Sri Vishwanath, son of Mallappa Kambar.
Based on these conclusions, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and determined a total compensation amount of Rs.63,80,160/-.

Recognizing that the deceased had contributed 50% to the accident, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.31,90,080/- along with interest at a rate of 6% per annum, effective from the date of the petition until the date of payment.
10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, petitioner-appellants have preferred this appeal for NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB enhancement of compensation.
The Insurance Company has also preferred appeal challenging the judgment and award questioning its liability.

Mahadevi vs Anil @ Anilkumar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156362189/
5 11.

The learned counsel representing the appellants has presented his arguments, contending that the Tribunal made an error by deducting 50% from the compensation due to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
It is asserted that the Tribunal failed to recognize that the accident was solely caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Moreover, the appellant's counsel argues that the rider of the motorcycle in question operated it recklessly and negligently, resulting in collision with the deceased's motorcycle.
This impact led to the deceased falling and sustaining severe injuries, ultimately leading to his demise.

13. The counsel emphasizes that PW2, an eyewitness to the accident, testified that the deceased was proceeding ahead of his motorcycle, and it was the rider of the motorcycle with registration No.KA-23/EJ-8649 who came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, leading to the collision.

The appellant's counsel maintains that the Tribunal - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB inadequately evaluated the evidence provided by PW2 and RW1 Furthermore, it is argued that the Tribunal failed to properly assess the deceased's income, as demonstrated in Exhibit P9, and accordingly, sought for allowing the appeal.

14. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has committed an error in coming to the conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-23/EJ-8649 in spite of evidence on record that the rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-23/EJ-8649 filed a compliant with the police stating that the deceased-Vishwanath himself was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed his motorcycle, which is evident from Exhibits P1 and P2.
The Tribunal has relied on the statement of objections filed in another connected case in MVC No.43 of 2017 without properly reading the said judgment.

The Tribunal has committed an error in not taking into consideration that the deceased- Vishwanath was riding the unnumbered motorcycle without possessing Driving Licence and charge sheeted under Sections 3 and 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

The Tribunal committed - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB an error in saddling liability on the Insurance Company in spite of evidence on record that the rider of the insured motorcycle filed MVC No.433 of 2017 for compensation, wherein the liability has been fixed on the petitioner No.1 by exonerating liability of the Insurance Company passed by the Senior Civil Judge, Raibagh through his Judgment dated 11th March, 2020.
He further submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in deducting one-fourth towards personal expenses.

Further, the Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence on record as to the dependency of the deceased; and on all these grounds, sought for allowing their appeal and to dismiss the appeal filed by the claimants.
12. Having heard the learned counsel on both sides and on perusal of records, the following points would arise for our consideration:
Mahadevi vs Anil @ Anilkumar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156362189/
6
1 . Whether the Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal?
2. Whether the claimants have made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB as to the liability as well as the quantum of compensation?
3. What order or award?

Based on the complaint lodged by Anilkumar Ramachandra Kambar, the Kudachi Police registered Crime No.89 of 2016 against accused No.1, Vishwanath Mallappa Kambar, on charges punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of the Indian Penal Code.
The resulting First Information Report was subsequently submitted to the appropriate Court.
In continuation, the police conducted a spot panchanama (inspection) at the location in question, with the presence of panchas (witnesses) as documented in Exhibit P3.
Additionally, the motor vehicles involved in the accident underwent examination by a Motor Vehicle Inspector.
To further establish facts, the Investigating Officer conducted an inquest panchanama, as documented in Exhibit P5, accompanied by - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB panchas.
As part of the investigation process, statements from witnesses were gathered.

Subsequently, based on meticulous investigation, the Investigating Officer filed a charge sheet against accused No.1, the deceased-Vishwanath Kambar, under Sections 278, 338 of the Indian Penal Code in conjunction with Sections 3 and 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, as documented in Exhibit P8.
15.
PW1-Mahadevi Vishwanath Kambar, testified that the accident resulted from the sole and rashly negligent driving of the motorcycle with registration No.KA-23/EJ-8649.
According to her testimony, this motorcycle was proceeding from the opposite direction and its rider was driving recklessly and negligently, thereby posing a threat to human life.
This rider abruptly lost control of the motorcycle and collided with Vishwanath's motorcycle, leading to the accident.

16. Similarly, RW1-the complainant Anil (also known as Anilkumar) Ramachandra Kambar,
provided his account of the incident.

He stated that during the accident, the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-23/M-0228 was coming from the opposite direction in a reckless and Mahadevi vs Anil @ Anilkumar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156362189/
7 negligent manner,
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB endangering human life.
According to his testimony, this rider suddenly lost control of the motorcycle and collided with his own motorcycle.
RW1 firmly believes that the accident was caused solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle ridden by Vishwanath Kambar.

17. Considering the evidence presented by both parties, the Tribunal had observed in paragraph 15 of the impugned judgment that, the Exhibits-P1, P2, and P8 had proven that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased-Vishwanath.
Consequently, a charge sheet was filed against him based on the complaint lodged by Anil with whose motorcycle the deceased's motorcycle collided with.

Respondent No.2, had therefore,
contended that it was not liable to pay compensation due to the accident being caused by the deceased Vishwanath's rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle.

However, it was revealed in the objection/Exhibit-P10 filed by the injured complainant, Anil, in the related MVC.No.433 of 2017,
arising from the same accident, that respondent No.2 had explicitly stated in paragraph No.14 that,

if the Tribunal determined the genuineness of the petition averments and the petitioner's - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB entitlement to compensation, then in such an event, 50% of the award should be allocated to the petitioner due to the contributory negligence on his part, as he had negligently come into contact with the vehicle.
This fact was also disclosed in the evidence affidavit of respondent No.2.

The implication is that the accident had occurred due to the contributory negligence of both the petitioner of MVC No.433 of 2017 (who is also the complainant) and the deceased-Vishwanath, in a ratio of 50:50.
This is further supported by respondent No.2's prayer in the aforementioned related case to allocate 50% compensation to the petitioner, Anil.
Therefore, it was determined that the accident had arisen from the contributory negligence of both deceased-Vishwanath and complainant Anil, who were operating the motorcycles.

Accordingly,
taking into account the contributory negligence and the types of motorcycles involved, liability was apportioned in the ratio of 50:50 between deceased-Vishwanath and complainant Anil.
Consequently, it was concluded that the petitioners had partially proven issue No.1, while the respondents had failed to substantiate issue No.2.
Thus, issue No.1 was answered partly in the AFFIRMATIVE, and issue No.2 in the NEGATIVE.

Upon careful analysis and re-evaluation of the evidence available, we have determined that there are no legal deficiencies or irregularities in the conclusion reached by the Tribunal, which assigned liability to both motorcycles in a 50:50 proportion.

8 19.
Regarding the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal had granted Rs.63,80,160/- for loss of dependency.

The counsel representing the appellant-claimants contended that the deceased Vishwanath, who was serving in Indian Army, earned a monthly salary of Rs.40,000/-,
substantiated by Exhibit P9, the Statement of Account for the Month ending February 2016.
However, upon thorough scrutiny of Exhibit P9, it was revealed that the deceased's salary was Rs.38,920/- and that there was no mention of Profession Tax, requiring a deduction of Rs.200/- per month.
Adjusting for Income Tax and Profession Tax, the monthly income would be Rs.36,856/-.

Pursuant to the Hon'ble Supreme Court's ruling in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI (2017 ACJ 2700), future prospects necessitate an addition of 50% to the notional income.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI (2017 ACJ 2700)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With three dependents, a quarter of the income must be subtracted for personal expenses of the - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB deceased.
After such adjustments, the deceased's monthly income would stand at Rs.41,463/-.

Consequently, the loss of dependency amounts to Rs.79,60,896/-
(Rs.41,463/- x 12 x 16).
Additionally, the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each for loss of consortium, leading to a total of Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 3).
The Claimants are also entitled for Rs.15,000/- each under the heads funeral expenses and loss of estate.

In the result, the claimants are entitled for compensation as under:

Towards loss of Dependency 79,60,896.00 2. Towards loss of Consortium 1,20,000.00 3. Towards loss of Estate 15,000.00 4. Towards Funeral Expenses 15,000.00  Total 81,10,896.00  Amount awarded by the Tribunal 63,80,160.00
Enhanced amount 17,30,736.00
Since there is contributory negligence of 50% by the deceased-Vishwanath, out of total compensation 50% has to be deducted.
Then the compensation comes to Rs.40,55,448, as against Rs.31,90,080/- awarded by the Tribunal.

In the result, we pass the following:
- 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9079-DB ORDER 1. Miscellaneous First Appeal No. 101782 of 2020 preferred by the Insurance Company is dismissed;

3. The judgment and award dated 05th March, 2020 passed in MVC No.2573 of 2017 by the XI Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi is modified by enhancing the compensation as above;

The Tribunal also found that the respondents failed to demonstrate that the accident had occurred exclusively due to the rash or negligent operation of the motorcycle with registration No.KA-23/M-0228.
Based on these conclusions, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and determined a total compensation amount of Rs.63,80,160/-.
Recognizing that the deceased had contributed 50% to the accident, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.31,90,080/- along with interest at a rate of 6% per annum, effective from the date of the petition until the date of payment.
The Tribunal has committed an error in not taking into consideration that the deceased- Vishwanath was riding the unnumbered motorcycle without possessing Driving Licence and charge sheeted under Sections 3 and 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Upon careful analysis and re-evaluation of the evidence available, we have determined that there are no legal deficiencies or irregularities in the conclusion reached by the Tribunal, which assigned liability to both motorcycles in a 50:50 proportion.
